questions.key_step: Use OC = 2(b - a) from hexagon geometry, then equate coefficients of independent vectors a, b.

questions.key_step: Every cross product of two sides at 60 degrees equals (sqrt3/2) l^2 n-hat, in the same direction.
questions.justification: Short chain: area of an equilateral triangle as a cross product, then ratio to the square's cross product; one familiar move with sign-checking from a figure.

questions.key_step: Dot with a to get the scalar a.x, then substitute it back into the given relation.
questions.justification: Routine elimination: dot product to get a scalar, substitute; a few standard steps, no insight needed.

questions.key_step: Use l^2+m^2+n^2=1 with the cross-term identity so the squared modulus collapses to (1 - sum l)^2.
questions.justification: Several stages (Lagrange identity cross terms, direction-cosine condition) with a hidden constraint; heavier algebra than a routine chain, but standard techniques.

questions.key_step: Common chord through the centre of the second circle gives c + d = 50; coplanarity of the lines gives lambda^2+3 lambda=0.
questions.justification: Two linked ideas (bisecting circles, then intersecting skew-line condition via a determinant) with a trap that two roots appear but only one is an option; like 2023-P2-Q4 but longer.

questions.key_step: Dot the given relation with a x b so only lambda|a x b|^2 survives; |b| comes from a.b=1 and the 60 degree angle.
questions.justification: Few routine steps: dot with a x b, Lagrange identity, find |b|; the 'none of these' option adds a small trap but no new idea.

questions.key_step: Reduce to 15 - 4(a.b+b.c+c.a) and use |a+b+c|^2 >= 0 to bound the bracket by -3/2.
questions.justification: Standard one-trick bound after routine expansion; the nonnegativity of |a+b+c|^2 is a familiar idea.

questions.key_step: Rectangle means a perpendicular b, so the given condition fixes the side ratio b = 3a.
questions.justification: Two stages: reduce the condition to a side ratio, then angle between diagonals via dot product and half-angle; routine but with sign/acute care.

questions.key_step: Dotting d with a, b, c kills two terms each time, leaving the triple product times one coefficient.

questions.key_step: The two triple products reduce to t^2 and 2t, giving t^2+2t=8.
questions.justification: Two standard identities lead to a quadratic; sign of t and tetrahedron factor 1/6 are the only traps.

questions.key_step: The given sum of squares makes |a+b+c|^2 = 0, so O is the centroid and OD = OC/2.
questions.justification: Single trick (sum of squared sides to |a+b+c|^2=0) followed by a median ratio; a few routine steps.

questions.key_step: The locus of a point dividing OA in a fixed ratio is the image of the locus of A under scaling about O.
questions.justification: Locus via scaling is a familiar idea, followed by a single line-plane intersection; routine multi-step 3D.

questions.key_step: Squaring b = lambda a + 3c gives a quadratic in lambda from the known lengths and a.c.
questions.justification: Routine dot-product chain (PDF) with a much shorter squaring route; no hidden idea.

questions.key_step: Combine the given inequality with |px - qy|^2 >= 0 to force p x = q y.
questions.justification: Non-routine: the equality-forcing inequality idea is not a standard coaching drill, but the algebra after it is short (comparable to anchors at L3).

questions.key_step: Direction cosines of d are equal, so each is plus or minus 1/sqrt3 and d.(a+b+c) = plus or minus sqrt3.
questions.justification: Standard direction-cosine fact and a short expansion; three or four routine steps.

questions.key_step: The coefficient matrix of u, v, w is the Gram matrix, whose determinant is [a b c]^2, so the volume is [a b c]^3.

questions.key_step: For unit vectors |a+b|^2 - |a-b|^2 over their sum is just cos(theta).

questions.key_step: Express |p|^2 and [p q r] in terms of sin^2(theta) by squaring the given relation, then take the range of sin^2(theta)/(1+sin^2(theta)).

questions.key_step: Gram determinant gives [a b c]^2 = 32; then height = volume / base area.

questions.key_step: Volume is 24[a b c]^2, so [a b c] = +-sqrt3/2; reduce the determinant with product-to-sum formulas.

questions.key_step: The coefficients ab cos(...) are dot products, so p + q = (a.b)c - (a.c)b = a x (c x b).

questions.key_step: All four conditions are standard equivalent forms of collinearity of three points.

questions.key_step: Equal cross products with b mean c - d is parallel to b, so d = c + mu b and b, c, d are coplanar.
